reconcile.note: Henry confines the legal bastard to offspring of the incestuous unions Leviticus 18 bans, letting an irregular birth like Jephthah's escape Deuteronomy 23:2's exclusion.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Wells counts only nine generations from the banned union of Judah and Tamar's son Pharez to David, arguing the royal genealogy breaches Deuteronomy 23:2's ten-generation exclusion.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (1999-2026), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: A bastard shall not enter into the assembly of Yahweh; even to the tenth generation shall none of his enter into the assembly of Yahweh.
sides.verseText: A bastard shall not enter into the assembly of Yahweh; even to the tenth generation shall none of his enter into the assembly of Yahweh.

sides.snippet: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.
sides.verseText: Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.
